source.title: Open problems on regular languages: an historical perspective

accepted.question_text: Fix a finite alphabet A, choose a basis B of languages over A, choose a collection of operations on languages, and choose rules governing how those operations may be applied. Which languages over A can be expressed from the basis B by using the chosen operations according to those rules?
accepted.context_brief: General expressibility problem for language-building systems

evidence.quote:
The aim of this paper is to discuss various instances of the following general problem.
Problem. Given a “basis” of languages, a set of operations and some rules
to use them, describe the languages expressible from the basis by using the
operations according to the rules.

accepted.question_text: An extended rational expression is built from letters using Boolean operations, concatenation, and the Kleene star, and the star-height of such an expression is the maximum nesting depth of star operations. The star-height of a regular language is the minimum star-height among all extended rational expressions defining it. Does there exist any regular language whose star-height is exactly 2, meaning that every defining extended rational expression requires nesting the star operation to depth at least 2?
accepted.context_brief: Existence of regular languages of star-height 2

evidence.quote:
The star-height of such an expression
is the maximum number of nested stars occurring in the expression.
The star-height of a language is the minimal star-height of an expression representing the language.

However, it is an open problem to know whether there are languages of
star-height 2.

accepted.question_text: For the Straubing-Thérien concatenation hierarchy of star-free languages over a finite alphabet A, level 0 consists of ∅ and A*, level n+1/2 consists of finite unions of marked products of languages from level n, and level n+1 consists of Boolean combinations of languages of marked products of level n. Given a half-integer n and a star-free language L, is there a decision procedure that determines whether L belongs to level n of this hierarchy?

evidence.quote:
The level 0
consists of the languages ∅ and A∗. The other levels are defined inductively
as follows:
(1) the level n+ 1/2 is the class of union of marked products of languages
of level n;
(2) the level n + 1 is the class of Boolean combination of languages of
marked products of level n.

Problem 2. Given a half integer n and a star-free language L, decide
whether L belongs to level n.

accepted.question_text: Consider lp-varieties of languages, meaning classes of recognizable languages that satisfy the variety closure conditions with inverse morphisms restricted to length-preserving morphisms. Is there a largest proper lp-variety of languages that is closed under the shuffle product?
accepted.context_brief: Largest proper lp-variety closed under shuffle

evidence.quote:
It would be interesting to know whether a similar result holds for lp￾varieties of languages: is there a largest proper lp-variety of languages closed
under shuffle?

accepted.question_text: Consider positive lp-varieties of languages, meaning lp-varieties that are not required to be closed under complement. Is there a largest proper positive lp-variety of languages that is closed under the shuffle product?
accepted.context_brief: Largest proper positive lp-variety closed under shuffle

evidence.quote:
Is there a largest proper positive lp-variety of languages
closed under shuffle?
